feedback: Penny's confession follows the available chain closely: she corrects her price-collar lie, explains the opening at the preview, and links the obtained poison to the unattended glass. Those actions were inferable beforehand; the confession confirms them rather than introducing a new decisive clue. The fact that she had already repaid the difference sharpens the motive without replacing it, since her earlier speech already said payment would not prevent exposure of the original betrayal. Her loss of control over her relatives' response is emotionally apt. Monet and Chip receive credible separate consequences, although all three speeches remain unusually orderly under pressure. The ending feels earned on the intended evidential standard.
